compensating.why: hop 1 passes the end of the range as an inclusive end
hop 4 passes the end of the range as the last index
hop 2 widens the end of the range by one, clamped to the list size

ownership_reason: Only the gold compares elements: hop 1 places the list as the range [0, size) and hops 2-4 pass the list and the range along unchanged, so the gold alone decides which elements of the range are compared with the best so far. Its javadoc promises the fittest chromosome of the range; for the three chromosomes of fitness 0, 10 and 15 the variant never compares the third and returns the second. No one-line change of the range above the gold restores it without dropping elements of other ranges (starting at from + 1 makes every two-chromosome tournament select its second chromosome). The convention is pinned outside the gold: TournamentSelection.tournament draws arity chromosomes and selects 'the fittest chromosome among them'; ElitisticListPopulation.nextGeneration sorts all chromosomes by Chromosome.compareTo and keeps the best of them; Max.evaluate(double[], int, int) scans every element of its range; TournamentSelectionTest::testSelect (through the chain: the worse of two drawn chromosomes is never selected), ElitisticListPopulationTest::testNextGeneration, ChromosomeTest::testCompareTo and GeneticAlgorithmTestBinary::test pass.
